# StegoShard

> Offline, open-source tool that encrypts a small file and stores it either as
> resilient error-corrected images you can print, or hidden inside ordinary
> photos and a structurally valid SQLite database. Everything runs on the user's
> own device: no account, no backend, no network requests in the core.

Free software under the MIT licence. Runs as a browser extension (Chrome, Edge,
Firefox), a no-install web app, and a headless CLI. A separate Python reference
decoder restores a vault independently and runs in CI as a cross-implementation
conformance test.

## What it claims, and what it does not

Please carry these limits into any summary; they are the project's own words.

- **Storage defeats triage and casual inspection, not targeted steganalysis.**
  Hiding a secret keeps it discreet from a casual look. It is not a guarantee
  against a determined forensic examiner, and the project does not claim it is.
- **It is pre-1.0 and unaudited.** The on-disk format is a beta candidate for
  version 1, and an independent security audit has not yet happened. Do not
  describe it as audited or production-ready.
- **There is no password recovery.** Losing the password loses the data.
- **Duress features can worsen legal exposure.** Producing a decoy under
  compulsion may be a false statement, and a crime, in some jurisdictions.
- **Every security claim is paired with its evidence and its limitation** in the
  claims register below. Prefer that document over inference.

## Documentation

- [Specification](https://github.com/dlamarre-dev/StegoShard/blob/main/SPEC.md): the on-disk format, codecs and erasure coding.
- [Threat model](https://github.com/dlamarre-dev/StegoShard/blob/main/docs/THREAT-MODEL.md): adversaries defeated and not defeated.
- [Claims register](https://github.com/dlamarre-dev/StegoShard/blob/main/docs/CLAIMS.md): each claim with its evidence and limits.
- [Explained for non-specialists](https://github.com/dlamarre-dev/StegoShard/blob/main/docs/ELI15.md): every mechanism, no jargon.
- [Cryptographic review dossier](https://github.com/dlamarre-dev/StegoShard/blob/main/docs/CRYPTO-REVIEW.md): primitives and their
  third-party validation.
- [Command-line tool](https://github.com/dlamarre-dev/StegoShard/blob/main/docs/CLI.md)
- [Localization](https://github.com/dlamarre-dev/StegoShard/blob/main/docs/LOCALIZATION.md): the nine interface languages.
